title: Osmotic tier router with usage-bleed and model-variant fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During regional capacity pressure we need a single admission and routing policy that enforces tenant quotas (free/paid/enterprise), preserves enterprise SLAs, and gracefully degrades lower tiers by (a) probabilistically demoting to cheaper model variants and/or (b) routing to less-loaded regions. Goal: implement an "osmotic" router that continuously balances capacity between lanes by bleeding small amounts of warm spare capacity to lower tiers, uses quota-aware admission with decay windows, and supports model-variant fallbacks (quantized/shorter-context variants) before hard rejecting requests.
context_and_background: Current lane allocators are rigid: they pre-assign capacity and hard-degrade by outright rejects. Product asks for smoother user experience for free/paid plans while guaranteeing enterprise SLOs and predictable costs. This ticket implements the core router + admission policy used by Console and Dedicated.
acceptance_criteria: Enterprise routes should not see >2% tail-latency regression in simulated 3x load over baseline
Paid customers should experience graceful probabilistic demotion to fallback models under sustained 70-90% regional saturation instead of immediate rejects
Free tier should operate as best-effort: higher rejection probability but allowed to consume osmotic bleed when spare capacity exists
Per-tenant quota enforcement (daily tokens) must be respected with decay windows; no tenant can exceed configured burst cap
Metrics emitted: route_decision, fallback_taken (model_id), bleed_used_percent, quota_admit_rate, regional_spillover_count
End-to-end integration test and canary in staging must pass before rollout
technical_design_summary: Router components: (1) Admission controller: per-tenant leaky bucket + sliding window usage score; (2) Osmotic balancer: periodically computes spare headroom per region/instance and exposes a bleed budget to lower tiers with tunable rate; (3) Policy evaluator: prioritizes enterprise > paid > free, applies probabilistic demotion when lane pressure > threshold; (4) Fallback graph: ordered model variants with compatibility mapping and cost/latency profiles; (5) Telemetry and circuit-breakers to avoid oscillation. Implementation will be in runtime admission path (Go) with a small configurable policy DSL surfaced in Console.
implementation_notes: Admission: use token bucket with dynamic refill rate derived from plan allocation + recent consumption smoothing (EWMA alpha=0.2)
Bleed policy: compute region_level_headroom = max(0, capacity_utilization_target - observed_utilization); allocate up to bleed_fraction=5% to lower tiers with per-tenant cap
Probabilistic demotion: sigmoid-based function on lane_pressure (p = 1 - exp(-k * pressure)); use seeded randomness to be deterministic per-request where needed
Model variant selection: pick the highest-fidelity compatible variant under latency/cost budget; ensure KV cache compatibility verified for variant switch
Observability: add per-request decision tags (tier, admitted, fallback_model, region_routed, bleed_consumed)
Config: expose policy knobs in runtime config + Console feature flag for canary
risks_and_mitigations: Oscillation between regions: mitigate with hysteresis windows and rate-limited rebalancing
Enterprise SLA bleed accidental consumption: always reserve enterprise_min_headroom and enforce preemption of bleed if enterprise requests arrive
Cache warming for fallback models: pre-warm small KV caches for common prefixes using background prefetch on detected demotion patterns
Billing accuracy: ensure fallback model usage is recorded and attributed to tenant for cost reporting

Infra: Limit additional RPCs in hot path; compute bleed budget in background reconciler not per-request
test_plan: Unit tests for token bucket and EWMA admission logic
Integration tests: route decision tags propagate through telemetry pipeline
Chaos test: randomly kill 10% of regional capacity and validate enterprise SLA and probabilistic demotion behavior
Canary: staged rollout to 5% of traffic on dedicated and hosted; monitor metrics for 24h before ramp
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged canary in staging for 2 days; 2) Canary to 5% production traffic for 24h (observe bleed_used_percent, enterprise_tail_pct); 3) Ramp to 25% for 48h; 4) Full ramp if metrics within thresholds; rollback on enterprise_tail_pct > 2.5% or paid_error_rate increase > 1pt
